_meta.title: The 23 delegations of the Apadana stair reliefs: their dress and gifts, for the court setting's petitioners and delegates (D-199; court setting only, D-003)
_meta.tiers: form B: the garments, headgear and footwear as the Apadana E and N stair reliefs carve them (APA-RELIEF), read through the standard identifications of the 23 delegations (Walser 1966, following Schmidt 1953's plates). NOT SEEN this session: the numbering, the identifications and every detail below are recollections of those publications and of photographs of the E stair (Livius, ISAC), to be verified against the plates (NEEDS_FROM_ME: Schmidt 1953 pls. 27-49, Walser 1966 Taf. 5-30). A detail the author is not sure of is marked (C) in its note. Read in full this session (HDT, Perseus): Herodotus' army list gives the Saka tall stiff caps tapering to a point, trousers, bows, daggers and axes (7.64), the Arabs girded mantles (7.69), the Thracians fox-skin caps, tunics, embroidered mantles and fawnskin shoes (7.75), the Bactrians a headgear like the Median (7.64), and the Egyptians shaven (2.36): claims about the army of 480 (B), used as support for the reliefs' forms. Colours C: the reliefs' paint is mostly lost (RELIEFS_AND_COLOUR); the natural dyes of D-189 (looks.ts DYES), chosen per people for plausibility, not from evidence. Gifts: the carved gifts (B), carried as the prop system allows (bowl, jar, cloth, basket, sack, spear); the animals (horses, camels, bulls, rams, a lioness, an okapi) and the chariots are NOT shown.
_meta.animals_d210: D-210 (gap audit item 17): `animal` = the animal the people's delegation leads on the Apadana reliefs, as the relief carving has it (src/arch/relief_figures.ts DELEGATIONS; B imagery, several RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN). In the court setting a delegation's party keeps it at the court's camp (activities.ts tend_animals variants: the horses, the Bactrian camel, the dromedary, the humped bull, the fat-tailed rams; the wild ass drawn with the donkey's form, C). The lioness with her cubs, the okapi and the ibex have no rig and are NOT drawn; the Lydians' and Libyans' chariots (RECOLLECTION) are not drawn either; those parties are seen with their pack animals.
_meta.numbering: Walser's Roman numerals for the E stair's N wing, counted from the stair's centre outward (recollection, NOT SEEN). Two identifications here follow the brief's list over Walser: XVII Sogdians (Walser: a second Saka group, the Sakā haumavargā, or the Sogdians; disputed) and XXI Cilicians (Walser: Drangianians; the Cilician identification is argued for another row by some; disputed). Q-370.
_meta.dress_keys: dress: the costume (outfits.ts COSTUMES: envoy = the long sleeved garment to the ankle, girt; envoy_short = the knee-length sleeved tunic, girt; envoy_bare = the wrap to the knee, bare above; median = the Median riding dress; persian = the Persian court robe); pieces: the optional pieces worn (always: every man of the people; the beard is chosen by `beard`); dyes: main, second and trim garment colours drawn from these lists (looks.ts DYES; C)

peoples.note: Median riding dress: rounded felt cap with neck flap, sleeved knee-length tunic, trousers, laced shoes; an akinakes; they bring vessels, a sword, bracelets and a set of clothes (B form; the laced shoes are drawn as the Median boots, C)

a long garment girt at the waist (close to the Persian robe: C), a fillet round the hair, shoes; they bring bows, daggers and a lioness with two cubs carried in the arms (the animals not shown; the bows and daggers carried as a bundle, C)
Median-type dress (soft cap, tunic, trousers, boots); a horse and the amphora with griffin handles (the horse not shown)
soft cap wrapped under the chin, tunic, trousers, boots; vessels, a skin and a two-humped camel (the camel not shown; the cap's chin wrap drawn as the Median cap, C)
a long garment to the ankle with a fringed shawl over it, a conical cap with a tassel hanging behind (the shawl and the tassel not modelled: C); cups, cloth and a humped bull (the bull not shown)
long garment and a mantle, a tall cap (the mantle not modelled; the cap drawn low, C); vessels, bowls, armlets and a two-horse chariot (the chariot not shown)
soft cap, tunic, trousers, boots (C: the cap is read by some as a wrapped headcloth); vessels, a skin and a camel (the camel not shown)
the Assyrians or Syrians: a long garment, a band round the hair (C); rams, cloth and bowls (the rams not shown)
Median-type dress with a mantle pinned at the shoulder (drawn as the kandys over the shoulders, C); a horse and garments (the horse not shown)

the E stair's Egyptian row is largely lost (only feet and hems survive: recollection, C for the whole figure): a long linen garment, shaven (Herodotus 2.36, B claim); the gifts are lost: calcite vessels as found in the Treasury (ISAC-FINDS, B) and linen stand in (C)

the pointed-cap Saka (Sakā tigraxaudā): tall pointed cap, knee-length tunic, trousers, boots, an akinakes (Herodotus 7.64: tall caps erect and stiff, tapering to a point, trousers, daggers and axes: B claim); a horse, armlets and a set of clothes (the horse not shown)
a long tunic (chiton) with a mantle, bareheaded (the mantle not modelled, C); cloth, bowls and balls of wool
knee-length tunic, trousers, boots, the hair bound with a band (C: Herodotus 7.64 gives the Bactrians in the army a headgear like the Median); bowls and a two-humped camel (the camel not shown)
short tunic and a cloak (the cloak not modelled), a band round the hair; spears, a round shield and a humped bull (the bull not shown; the shield carried as a bundle, C)
Median-type dress; vessels and a two-humped camel (the camel not shown)
Median-type riding dress; a horse and garments (the horse not shown)
the identification is disputed (a second Saka group for some: Q-370); soft cap with flaps, tunic, trousers, boots, an akinakes; a horse, axes and swords (the horse not shown)

gifts: baskets with jars on a yoke
peoples.note: bare above the waist, a wrap to the knee, bare feet or sandals, a band round the hair; baskets with jars carried on a yoke (the yoke not modelled), axes and an ass (the ass not shown)

the Skudra (Thracians): tunic, cloak, boots, a cap (Herodotus 7.75: fox-skin caps and fawn-skin boots, B claim; the cloak not modelled; the cap drawn low, C); spears, shields and a horse (the horse not shown)
a long garment girt at the waist (Herodotus 7.69: the Arabs' long girded mantles, B claim), a band round the hair; cloth and a dromedary (the dromedary not shown)
the identification is disputed (Walser: Drangianians; Q-370): knee-length tunic, a cap, shoes (C); rams, bowls and cloth (the rams not shown)
a long garment or cloak open at the front (drawn closed, C), bareheaded; a spear, a kudu antelope and a two-horse chariot (the antelope and the chariot not shown)
the Ethiopians (Kushites): a long wrapped garment, short hair; an elephant's tusk, a lidded vessel and an okapi or giraffe (the animal not shown; the tusk carried as a bundle on the shoulder, C)
